verdict: Intel grew revenue 7% to $13.6B with data-center sales up 22% — but a $4,070M restructuring line, mostly a non-cash $3.9B goodwill impairment, drove a $4,281M total net loss.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, attributable to Intel; non-GAAP EPS was $0.29

kpis.label: Data Center and AI
kpis.note: +22% YoY — the growth engine this quarter

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Server CPUs and AI products for datacenters. Up 22% YoY on higher server prices and demand.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Chip manufacturing for outside customers only (most Foundry revenue is internal and eliminated on consolidation).

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mostly Mobileye ($558M of it), plus smaller businesses; down 33% YoY mainly because Altera was deconsolidated in 2025.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new CPUs, AI accelerators and process technology; down from $3,640M a year ago.

opex.name: Marketing, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and back-office costs; down from $1,177M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring and other charges
opex.note: Mostly a $3,965M asset impairment charge — including about $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment — plus $74M of severance and $31M of litigation and other charges; Intel excludes these from non-GAAP results.

follow100Note: One line dominates: restructuring and impairments took $29.98 of every $100 of revenue. Without that line, the quarter would have been operating-profitable.
otherDetail: Other expense of $810M net combines two lines: interest and other, net of -$738M — which includes a $1,090M mark-to-market loss on the U.S. government Escrowed Shares — and a $72M loss on equity investments. Of the $4,281M total net loss, $553M was attributable to non-controlling interests, leaving $3,728M attributable to Intel.
footerNote: Net loss attributable to Intel was $3,728M (EPS -$0.73); the $4,281M total includes $553M attributable to non-controlling interests.

takeaways.title: Data center is carrying growth
takeaways.text: Data Center and AI revenue rose 22% to $5,052M on higher server prices and demand, while client computing was roughly flat at $7,727M. Total revenue rose 7% to $13,577M and gross margin improved to 39.4% from 36.9%.

takeaways.title: A goodwill impairment drove the loss
takeaways.text: Restructuring and other charges were $4,070M, of which $3,965M was asset impairments — including about $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment — versus just $156M of total charges a year ago. Excluding one-offs, non-GAAP EPS was a profit of $0.29.

takeaways.title: Cash held up, guidance rose
takeaways.text: Intel generated $1,096M of operating cash flow despite the paper charges, repurchased the 49% minority stake in its Fab 34 Ireland venture, and guided Q2 revenue to $13.8B–$14.8B.

oneTimers: Asset impairment charges: $3,965M inside restructuring — including about $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment — plus $74M of severance and $31M of litigation and other charges.
Mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares: $1,090M inside 'interest and other, net' — a non-cash charge linked to the U.S. government CHIPS Act share agreement; Intel excludes it from non-GAAP results.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Mar 28, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)
